# Integral Jensen graphs: the kernel-module criterion and a complete 13-point certificate

Let P be a finite lattice-convex subset of Z^k. A function g:P->R is Jensen-affine if it preserves every convex representation landing in P. Write L(P) for this finite-dimensional space. Given rational g in L(P), define

    P_g = {z in P : g(z) is an integer},
    T_g = {(z,g(z)) : z in P_g} subset Z^(k+1).

The general bound h(T_g)<=2^k is now refuted by the separate eleven-point certificate `candidate 5c9190df7c42c598`. The present note proves an exact arithmetic criterion for a proposed Helly witness and shows that the archived connected 13-point example cannot refute the bound, for ANY rational g in its entire Jensen space. This includes every rational affine correction and every modulus, not merely the originally displayed mode.

## 1. Integer graph points and the correct Helly kernel

The convex hull of T_g has precisely T_g as its integer points. Indeed an integer point (z,t) of this hull projects to z in conv(P) intersect Z^k = P. Its convex representation from T_g gives t=g(z) by Jensen affinity. Since t is integer, z belongs to P_g.

More generally, for every V subset P and p in P,

    p in conv(V)
      iff (p,g(p)) in conv{(v,g(v)):v in V}.              (1)

The forward direction is Jensen affinity and the reverse is projection.

For a finite W of distinct points define its deletion kernel

    K(W) = intersection_(w in W) conv(W minus {w}).       (2)

For a finite source set S, its Helly number is exactly the largest cardinality of a subset W of S satisfying

    K(W) intersect S = empty.                            (3)

Here is a short proof of the characterization. If (3) holds, the convex sets conv(W minus {w}) have empty full intersection with S, but every subfamily missing the set indexed by w contains w. Conversely, for a minimal S-infeasible family C_1,...,C_m choose w_i in S intersect intersection_(j!=i) C_j. The w_i are distinct, and conv(W minus {w_i}) subset C_i, giving (3). Since S is finite, every infeasible family has a finite infeasible subfamily: choose for each point of S one set excluding it.

A witness W in (3) must be in convex position. Otherwise some w belongs to conv(W minus {w}), and w belongs to every other deletion hull because it is one of their generating points. Also, if V subset W with |V|>=2, then

    K(V) subset K(W).                                    (4)

For a deleted w outside V use K(V) subset conv(V); for w in V use its own deletion hull. Thus to rule out h(S)>b, it suffices to rule out witnesses of size b+1.

By (1), if W subset P_g, the exact witness condition for its lifted graph is

    g(p) is noninteger for EVERY p in P intersect K(W).  (5)

The test concerns the deletion kernel, not the whole convex hull. Points of S in conv(W) but outside K(W) do not by themselves defeat a Helly witness.

## 2. An exact integer-module obstruction

Choose a rational basis of L(P), clear its coordinate denominators, and encode it by integer feature rows A_p in Z^ell, p in P. Thus every rational Jensen function has the form

    g(p)=alpha dot A_p,   alpha in Q^ell.

For a candidate W subset P, put

    Lambda_W = span_Z{A_w:w in W}.

If some p in P intersect K(W) satisfies

    A_p in Lambda_W,                                    (6)

then W cannot be an integral-graph Helly witness for ANY such g. Integrality at W forces integrality at p by the integer linear combination in (6), contradicting (5).

Consequently a finite certificate of one witness (6) for every convex-position (b+1)-subset proves h(T_g)<=b simultaneously for every rational g in L(P).

There is also an exact converse formulation for any fixed candidate W, which tracks the possible need to exclude several kernel points simultaneously. Set

    Lambda = span_Z{A_p:p in P},  G_W=Lambda/Lambda_W,
    B_W = {[A_p] in G_W : p in P intersect K(W)}.

Then some rational g makes W a graph Helly witness if and only if there exists a finite-order character

    chi:G_W -> Q/Z

which is nonzero on EVERY member of B_W. A rational coefficient vector induces such a character. Conversely every finite-order character pulls back to a rational functional on the free lattice Lambda, hence is represented by some rational alpha on its real span. Its zero set is exactly the desired integrality filter on P. This criterion is independent of a choice of integer feature basis. For actual deletion-kernel points, every class in B_W is torsion: p in K(W) implies p in conv(W), and Jensen affinity gives A_p as a rational convex combination of A_W (rational coefficients can be chosen because all rows are rational). Clearing denominators places a positive integer multiple of A_p in Lambda_W. Thus the free-part discussion below is valid but unnecessary for actual kernel witnesses; only a finite torsion-character search is required.

An individual nonzero witness class is always separable by a finite-order character, but several classes need not be simultaneously separable. Thus failure of (6) for each separate p is not itself a counterexample.

For completeness this is a finite arithmetic decision after separating the free part. Write G_W = Z^r direct-sum F, with F finite. A separating character exists if and only if some character of F is nonzero on every element of B_W having zero free coordinate. Necessity is immediate. For sufficiency choose a prime p larger than the number of remaining elements, coprime to |F|, and not dividing all coordinates of any of their nonzero free vectors. A linear functional on (Z/pZ)^r can be chosen outside their finitely many proper hyperplanes. Its values divided by p are nonzero on all those vectors and cannot cancel the chosen F-character because the orders are coprime. The torsion character search is finite. Smith normal form therefore gives an exact test without relying on a cutoff in moduli.

## 3. The archived connected 13-point configuration

Use the lattice-convex P from `candidate e3932c47b953f7cd`, with this zero-based index table:

    i     p_i       g_0(p_i)
    0   (0,0,1)       0
    1   (0,0,2)       0
    2   (0,0,3)       0
    3   (0,1,1)       3
    4   (0,1,2)       3
    5   (0,1,3)       3
    6   (0,2,1)       6
    7   (1,0,0)       0
    8   (1,0,1)       0
    9   (1,1,0)       0
   10   (1,1,1)       1
   11   (1,2,0)       0
   12   (2,0,0)       0

The defining inequalities are

    x,y,z>=0, x+z>=1,
    x+2y+z<=5, 2x+y+z<=4, 3x+2z<=6.                     (7)

All integer points satisfying (7) appear in the table. Every point is on the boundary of this polytope. The archived proof gives

    L(P)=span{1,x,y,z,g_0},   dim L(P)=5.                (8)

The exact verifier independently confirms (8): it enumerates valid two- and three-source convex representations, finds relation rank eight, and checks that all five displayed independent columns satisfy every enumerated relation. The archived affinity-on-minimal-faces argument supplies that g_0 preserves all anchored representations.

Set A_i=(1,p_i,g_0(p_i)). The ONLY convex-position nine-subsets of P are

    W_1={1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9,10},
    W_2={1,2,3,5,6,7,8,10,11},
    W_3={1,2,3,5,6,7,9,10,12},
    W_4={1,2,3,5,6,8,9,10,11}.                         (9)

This small finite assertion has a complete exact rational verifier, described below; no floating-point hull computation enters the certificate.

Every W in (9) contains {1,2,3,5,6} and omits 4. Two disjoint midpoint representations give

    p_4=(p_2+p_6)/2=(p_3+p_5)/2.                        (10)

After deleting ANY one point of W, at least one of these midpoint pairs remains. Therefore

    p_4 in K(W).                                        (11)

Finally the integer feature identity is

    A_4=A_3+A_2-A_1.                                    (12)

It can be checked coordinate by coordinate. Hence every rational Jensen function satisfies

    g(p_4)=g(p_3)+g(p_2)-g(p_1).

If all points of W have integer heights, p_4 has integer height as well. Equations (11)--(12) are the required unavoidable integer kernel witness.

**Theorem for this configuration.** For every rational g in the full L(P),

    h(T_g)<=8=2^3.                                      (13)

Indeed a larger Helly witness would have a nine-subset by (4), would have to be in convex position, hence would be one of (9), and would be defeated by its integral kernel point p_4. Empty or smaller filtered sets cause no issue.

## 4. Exact finite verification and scope

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_integral_jensen_graph_thirteen_point_helly.py` uses only Python integer arithmetic and Fraction. It:

1. enumerates the integer points from (7), and verifies that all are on its boundary;
2. lists every positive two- or three-source representation landing in a different P point by Cramer's rule, verifying all four homogeneous base coordinates exactly;
3. checks the relation rank and the five Jensen feature columns;
4. enumerates all 715 nine-subsets, rejecting one whenever it contains an anchored point and one of its source sets;
5. obtains exactly the four sets (9), and verifies (10)--(12).

Why source supports of size at most three suffice: every p in P lies in a face of dimension at most two. Every representation landing at p uses its minimal face; planar Caratheodory then reduces to at most three affinely independent sources. Thus the enumeration is complete for convex position, not a screen over selected relations.

The verifier passes. The new general ingredient is the simultaneous character/kernel criterion in Section 2. The 13-point theorem rules out all modular variants of this one archived connected example. It does not establish the general bound h(T_g)<=2^k for arbitrary P; that bound is false by the separate eleven-point certificate cited above. It does not imply the original sharp mixed-depth inequality.
